Rupee Fluctuates Against US Dollar Amid Oil Prices and Geopolitical Concerns

The Indian Rupee saw fluctuations against the US dollar in early trade, with one report stating it rose 14 paise to 95.85, while another reported a fall of 26 paise to 95.99. Forex traders cited persistent dollar demand from domestic importers, particularly oil companies, elevated crude oil prices, and broad-based strength in the US dollar index as factors influencing the currency. Geopolitical uncertainties and selling in domestic equity markets also contributed to the rupee's weakening, according to one report.
